DEATHWARD / IMPLEMENTATION AUDIT

Isaac regular enemies: what is actually implemented?

This report names the Isaac enemy behind each entry, shows current runtime configuration, and preserves the distinction between code existing and a faithful port being fully accepted.

Read this before interpreting the counts. Variants and subtypes are separate records, not separate enemy families. “Partial implementation” means behavior work is recorded; it does not mean all behavior, interactions, balance or visuals match Isaac. “No runtime definition” means no direct monster entry was found; an entity may still need a producer/component route. No completion percentage is invented.

Scope and evidence

The default view includes reviewed regular enemies plus unreviewed enemy candidates. Bosses, reviewed support entities, hazards and exclusions remain accessible through the scope selector, so uncertain classification is visible rather than silently discarded.

Validation badges show recorded evidence, not a fresh test of every row. A partial result remains partial. Historical Linux/browser checks may describe older builds; inspect each evidence scope and report. WASM checks are waived by the user. Current screenshots are DeathWard captures; they are not controlled side-by-side Isaac gameplay comparisons.

Data authority: current assets/mechanics/*.mechanics supplies runtime definitions. Maintained checklist notes supply review decisions and gaps. The original research catalog supplies Isaac identity and source HP; its older DeathWard snapshot is deliberately not used for current stats. Registered HP is base tuning; stage rules and runtime modifiers can change actual HP. A “legacy” graph may dispatch to a dedicated family controller; the graph name alone does not prove generic or faithful AI.

Regular enemies can be playable while champion modifiers or shared item/status interactions remain unfinished. Those gaps prevent full acceptance; they do not imply ordinary movement and attacks are absent. Appearance is DeathWard’s own 3D adaptation.
